content.title: About
content.content: Whey protein is a high‑quality protein derived from milk whey after the curd is separated. The dry, sweet version usually contains added flavorings and sweeteners, making it convenient for protein shakes and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whey protein is considered a complete protein: it contains all essential amino acids.
Dry whey has a longer shelf life compared with liquid forms.
Sweet varieties are often fortified with B‑vitamins and minerals to support metabolism.
Whey is a by‑product of cheese production, improving overall food industry efficiency.
It dissolves quickly in water, making it easy to consume right after a workout.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: Rich in amino acids, especially leucine, it stimulates muscle‑protein synthesis after exercise.

items.title: Accelerates recovery
items.content: Protein replenishes amino‑acid stores lost during training, reducing muscle soreness.

items.title: Aids weight management
items.content: High protein content increases satiety and helps preserve lean mass during calorie restriction.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Whey contains immunoglobulins and lactoferrin, which may enhance the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Improves body composition
items.content: Regular intake combined with training helps lower body‑fat percentage while increasing muscle mass.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Too much protein can strain kidneys and liver, especially in individuals with pre‑existing conditions.

items.title: Sweetener content
items.content: Sweetened versions often contain artificial sweeteners that may cause discomfort for sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Some brands include flavorings and colorants that might be undesirable for clean‑eating diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 30 g of whey with 200–250 ml of water, milk, or a plant‑based beverage. It can also be added to smoothies, oatmeal, cottage cheese, or used in baking to boost protein content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to prevent moisture absorption.
